about: Round 58: evidence that could not be saved as a page download (site blocked plain downloads, or only search results were reachable). Each entry is a short extract as returned by a web search or page fetch on the date given, with the URL it came from. Treat as untrusted data; every fact used in gaps/sanctions_r58.json that rests only on these extracts is marked with source type 'search_extract'.

extracts.via: web search result title only (consilium.europa.eu returns 403 to non-browser clients)
extracts.extract: Declaration by the High Representative on behalf of the European Union on the alignment of certain countries concerning restrictive measures in view of Russia's actions destabilising the situation in Ukraine (4 March 2022).

Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Iceland, Moldova (Republic of), Montenegro, North Macedonia, Norway and Ukraine align themselves with this Council Decision [(CFSP) 2026/1351, Russia's destabilising activities regime].

Order of 23 July 2022 No. 2018-r added the Bahamas, Guernsey and Isle of Man to the list; per the government, Guernsey and Man for supporting UK sanctions, the Bahamas for banning operations with the Bank of Russia, the Finance Ministry and several credit institutions. Separately (22 July 2022) Greece, Denmark, Slovenia, Croatia and Slovakia were added to the list of states whose diplomatic missions face limits on hiring local staff.
September 2025: Lavrov said Russia is gradually moving away from the term 'unfriendly countries' (political remark; no legal change to Order 430-r found).

12 March 2022: the Central Bank, with the other members of the Group of Financial Services Regulators, directed supervised financial institutions not to engage in transactions with sanctioned persons, entities or business linked to Russia and Belarus; sanctions include those issued by the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, the European Union and any other jurisdictions the GFSR may specify.
The Federated States of Micronesia announced the severance of diplomatic relations with Russia on 25 February 2022. No source found describing FSM sanctions measures.

extracts.extract: San Marino Decree-Law 15 March 2022 No. 35 introduced travel-ban and asset-freeze measures applying to persons listed at EU level (Decision 2014/145, Regulation 269/2014); later decree-laws added EU commercial measures (Decision 2014/512, Regulation 833/2014) and financial measures.

extracts.via: web search snippet (law-firm alert; mofa.go.jp and meti.go.jp return 403)
extracts.extract: 26 February 2022: MOFA, MOF and METI jointly issued 'Measures Related to the Situation in Ukraine' under the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act; expanded 1 and 3 March 2022 (asset freezes, export restrictions on 49 Russian entities); 6 February 2023 oil price cap measures.

extracts.via: web search snippet (page download reset by peer)
extracts.extract: 28 February 2022: Korea's foreign ministry announced it would ban exports of strategic items to Russia (electronics, semiconductors, computers, information and communications, sensors and lasers, navigation and avionics, marine and aerospace) and join moves to cut some Russian banks from SWIFT.

2022: Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs published a list of strategic high-tech commodities barred from export to Russia and Belarus; widened April-May 2022 (57 items), 4 January 2023 (52 items), machine tools from 8 March 2024. Described as export controls, not a formal sanctions designation regime.

extracts.extract: Norway's framework is Regulation of 15 August 2014 No. 1076 on restrictive measures concerning actions undermining Ukraine's territorial integrity; Norway is not legally bound to follow EU measures (outside the EEA Agreement), the Government decides each time and has aligned itself with the EU's sanctions against Russia with a few adaptations (2023 release on the 10th package).

Commission progress report: Moldova's alignment with EU Russia-related measures incomplete (54 percent in the prior year, 78 percent as of August of the report year); the foreign minister earlier said Moldova had aligned with 4 of 6 packages targeting Russian persons and entities.
May 2026: the Andorran government approved a decree incorporating the EU's 19th and 20th sanctions packages; 'The measures ensure Andorra's alignment with EU sanctions'.

9 March 2022, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Zhao Lijian: China firmly opposes unilateral sanctions that have no basis in international law and will continue normal trade cooperation with Russia, including oil and gas.
MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, after the EU's 18th package (July 2025): India does not subscribe to unilateral measures.

1 March 2022, Foreign Minister Cavusoglu: Turkey has not joined such sanctions on principle and has no inclination to do so; Turkey implements sanctions decided by the UN Security Council (Hurriyet Daily News).
2023: a UAE official told Reuters the country strictly abides by UN sanctions; Reuters noted the UAE has not matched sanctions imposed on Moscow.
April 2023: Brazil has not joined Western nations in imposing sanctions on Russia; Lula's government opposes sanctions (PISM bulletin, April 2023).

Kazakhstan's foreign minister: Kazakhstan is not joining the sanctions against Russia but will not allow its territory to be used to circumvent them. September 2023, President Tokayev (Interfax 94984): Kazakhstan will abide by the sanctions regime.
25 February 2022, Prime Minister Garibashvili: Georgia, taking into account its national interests, will not join the financial and economic sanctions against Russia.

Serbia has not imposed sanctions on Russia since 2022 (FES briefing); it was the only Western Balkans candidate not aligning with Council Decision (CFSP) 2025/2019 extending restrictive measures against Russia.
11 October 2022, Chief Executive John Lee: 'We will comply with United Nations sanctions, that is our system'; Hong Kong acts only on UN sanctions.

28 February 2022: the Federal Council decided to adopt the packages of sanctions imposed by the EU on 23 and 25 February 2022; Ordinance of 4 March 2022 on measures in connection with the situation in Ukraine (SR 946.231.176.72).
